text: For the choirmaster. A psalm of David,
when Nathan the prophet came to him after he had gone in to Bathsheba.
Have mercy on me, O God, according to your steadfast love; in your great compassion blot out my transgressions.
Wash me thoroughly from my guilt, and cleanse me from my sin.
For I know my transgressions, and my sin is always before me.
Against you, you alone, have I sinned, and done what is evil in your sight, so that you are just when you speak and blameless when you judge.
Indeed, I was born in guilt; in sin my mother conceived me.
Surely you delight in truth deep within; so teach me wisdom in the hidden place.

versions.text: You delight in truth in the inmost being; so teach me wisdom deep within.
versions.explanation: The opening particle הֵן ("behold, surely") is rendered in verse 7 ("Indeed") but dropped here, weakening the parallel between the two verses. Also, "deep within" currently renders the second colon (בְסָתֻם), while the first colon (בַטֻּחוֹת) is given the heavier phrase "the inmost being"; balancing the two cola reads more smoothly aloud.

text: Cleanse me with hyssop, and I will be clean; wash me, and I will be whiter than snow.
Let me hear joy and gladness; let the bones you have crushed rejoice.
Hide your face from my sins, and blot out all my guilt.
Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me.
Do not cast me from your presence, and do not take your holy Spirit from me.

versions.text: Do not cast me from your presence, and do not take your Holy Spirit from me.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew רוּחַ קָדְשְׁךָ is simply "your holy spirit/breath." Full capitalization imports a developed Trinitarian reading into the psalm; lowercase "holy" (or a footnote noting "or: your holy spirit") keeps the original sense while leaving the fuller reading open.

text: Restore to me the joy of your salvation, and sustain me with a willing spirit.
Then I will teach transgressors your ways, and sinners will return to you.
Deliver me from bloodguilt, O God, God of my salvation, and my tongue will sing of your righteousness.
Lord, open my lips, and my mouth will declare your praise.
For you take no delight in sacrifice, or I would bring it; you are not pleased with burnt offerings.
The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and crushed heart, O God, you will not despise.

versions.text: The sacrifice God desires is a broken spirit; a broken and crushed heart, O God, you will not despise.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is plural ("the sacrifices of God"), and the verb "desires" is supplied rather than present in the text. Keeping the plural construct preserves the contrast with the plural sacrifices of verses 18 and 21.

text: In your good pleasure do good to Zion; rebuild the walls of Jerusalem.
Then you will delight in right sacrifices, in burnt offerings and whole offerings; then bulls will be offered on your altar.
